initial_requirements: MultiMahjong is a computer version of Mahjong for both networked and standalone play. Up to four people should be able to join a shared game through client applications connected to a game server. When fewer human players are available, the application should provide computer-controlled opponents so that a user can still start and complete a valid game.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What are the primary goals and success criteria for MultiMahjong from the stakeholder’s perspective—for example, what should the system enable for players, and how will you judge whether the project is successful?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
The main goal is to let people play a proper game of Mahjong on a computer, whether they’re all online together or someone is playing alone against computer opponents. It should be easy to start a game, support up to four players, and still produce a complete valid match even if not all seats are filled by humans.
I’d judge it successful if players can reliably join a shared game through the client, play through an entire Mahjong session without the system breaking the rules of the game, and have the experience feel smooth enough that they can actually finish a match. If single-player or partially filled games work well with the computer-controlled opponents, that would also be a key sign it met the business need.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Who are the key stakeholder roles for MultiMahjong, and what responsibilities or interests does each role have in the system?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
The key roles are the players, who want to join games, play Mahjong smoothly, and have the rules enforced correctly. Then there’s the game host or server operator, who cares that games can be created, managed, and kept stable for multiple clients at once.
I’d also include whoever is responsible for the computer-controlled opponents, because they need to behave well enough to keep a game playable when there aren’t four humans. On our side, the development or support team would care about reliability, troubleshooting, and making sure the networking and standalone modes both work as intended.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What are the main functional capabilities MultiMahjong must provide from start to finish—for example, game setup, player joining/leaving, turn handling, move validation, scoring, chat or other in-game actions, and ending/restarting a match?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
At a minimum, it needs to let someone start a new Mahjong game, have up to four players join it, and fill any missing seats with computer opponents so the game can still proceed. Once the match is underway, it has to manage turns, enforce legal moves, and keep all clients in sync with the current game state.
It should also handle a player leaving without crashing the session, as gracefully as possible, though I’d want to verify exactly what the expected behavior is there. At the end of a match, it needs to determine the result, show the outcome to the players, and allow a new game to be started afterward.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Which Mahjong rule set and scoring/win conditions should MultiMahjong follow, and do you want to support any rule variants or regional differences (for example, differing tile sets, allowed melds, winning hands, or scoring rules)?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
I don’t have that nailed down yet, so I’d need to verify which Mahjong variant the team wants as the baseline. My assumption would be that we should pick one standard rule set first and make sure it plays correctly end to end, rather than trying to support multiple regional variants up front.
If we do add variants later, I’d expect that to be a separate scope decision because tile sets, winning hands, and scoring can change a lot between rule sets. For now, I’d treat that as an open requirement.

turns.interviewer_utterance: To define the baseline Mahjong behavior, which specific rule set or regional variant should MultiMahjong use, and what are the key business rules for winning, scoring, and declaring a completed hand or match under that rule set?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
We haven’t locked that down yet, so I can’t honestly name a specific regional variant today. For requirements purposes, I’d want us to choose one baseline standard before implementation, because the win conditions and scoring depend too much on the exact rules to leave ambiguous.
If I had to state the business rule at a high level right now, it would be that a hand is completed when a player forms a legal winning Mahjong hand under the selected rule set, and the match ends according to that rule set’s scoring and round structure. I’d need to confirm the exact tile set, legal melds, and point calculation with the product owner or domain expert before we can freeze that requirement.

turns.interviewer_utterance: For the baseline Mahjong rule set, what exact tile set should MultiMahjong use, how should the scoring model calculate points, and what rules should govern seat assignment and dealer rotation at the start of a game?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
I don’t have those exact details approved yet, so I can’t give you a definitive tile set or scoring formula from the stakeholder side. My expectation is that we’d define one standard four-player tile set and a single scoring model for the first release, then keep seat assignment and dealer rotation consistent with that standard so the game starts predictably every time.
For now, I’d say the system should assign seats automatically or let players join into available seats, then determine the dealer at the start and rotate it according to the chosen rule set after each hand. The exact point values and tile composition still need confirmation before we can treat them as fixed requirements.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What criteria should we use to choose the baseline Mahjong rule set for MultiMahjong—for example, should it prioritize a widely recognized standard, ease of implementation, availability of authoritative rules, or alignment with the intended player audience?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
I’d prioritize a widely recognized standard that’s well documented and practical to implement first. The biggest factors for me would be clear authoritative rules, low ambiguity for the development team, and a good fit for the audience we expect to play the game.
If there’s a tradeoff, I’d rather choose the variant that lets us deliver a complete, reliable product sooner than one that is more niche or complicated. If the intended audience strongly expects a particular regional style, though, that would become the deciding factor.

turns.interviewer_utterance: If a player disconnects or leaves during an active game, what should MultiMahjong do with the current game state—should the seat be reserved for possible rejoin, replaced immediately by an AI or another player, and should the match pause, continue, or be ended in each case?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
My preference would be to keep the seat reserved for a short reconnection window so the player can rejoin without disrupting the match. If they do not come back in time, then the system should replace them with an AI opponent so the game can continue to completion.
I would not want the whole match to end just because someone disconnects, unless the remaining game state becomes invalid under the chosen rules. Pausing could be useful briefly for a reconnect, but after that it should continue rather than stall indefinitely.

turns.interviewer_utterance: When a player disconnects, what specific reconnection timeout should the system use, and how should the match behave during that window—should gameplay pause or continue, and what exact state transition should occur when the timeout expires and an AI takes over the seat?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
I don’t have a fixed timeout agreed yet, so I’d treat that as something we still need to set. My instinct would be a short reconnection window, something on the order of a couple of minutes, but that’s just a starting point and not a final requirement.
During that window, I’d prefer the match to pause briefly if the disconnected player is the active one, so we don’t force irreversible actions. If the timeout expires, the seat should transition from reserved-for-reconnect to AI-controlled, and the game should resume from the current state with no restart.

turns.interviewer_utterance: When a player disconnects during their turn and the match pauses for reconnection, what exact state should be preserved and what actions, if any, should be blocked or allowed so the game can resume fairly if they return or safely continue if an AI takes over?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
We’d need to preserve the full live game state at that moment, including the current tile wall or draw state, each player’s hand, exposed melds, discard history, turn order, dealer status, and any pending action windows like a claim opportunity. That way the reconnecting player comes back to exactly the same point and nothing is lost.
While paused, I’d block any new turn advancement or irreversible decisions, but I’d still want the system to keep the state ready for a clean resume. If the timeout expires and AI takes over, the game should continue from that preserved state without changing the underlying hand state, just changing who controls that seat.

slots.name: project_goals
slots.value: Enable people to play a proper computer-based Mahjong game in either networked multiplayer or solo/partial-player mode with computer-controlled opponents; support easy game start, up to four players, and completion of a valid full match. Success is judged by reliable client joining, uninterrupted rule-correct play through an entire session, a smooth experience, and effective computer opponents when human seats are unfilled.

slots.name: stakeholder_roles
slots.value: Players who want to join games, play smoothly, and have rules enforced correctly; a game host or server operator who manages and keeps multiplayer games stable; whoever is responsible for the computer-controlled opponents so they behave well enough to keep games playable; and the development/support team focused on reliability, troubleshooting, and ensuring both networking and standalone modes work as intended.

slots.name: functional_needs
slots.value: The system must let a user start a new Mahjong game, allow up to four players to join, fill any missing seats with computer-controlled opponents, manage turns, enforce legal moves, keep all clients synchronized with current game state, handle a player leaving without crashing the session as gracefully as possible, determine and present the match result at the end, and allow a new game to be started afterward.

slots.name: business_rules
slots.value: A hand is completed when a player forms a legal winning Mahjong hand under the selected rule set, and the match ends according to that rule set’s scoring and round structure. The exact tile set, legal melds, and point calculation are not yet finalized and must be confirmed with the product owner or domain expert.

slots.name: data_entities
slots.value: Full live game state must be preserved for reconnection, including the current tile wall or draw state, each player’s hand, exposed melds, discard history, turn order, dealer status, and any pending action windows such as claim opportunities.

slots.name: constraints
slots.value: The first release should use one standard four-player tile set and a single scoring model; seat assignment should be automatic or allow joining available seats, and dealer rotation should follow the chosen rule set. Exact tile composition and point values still need confirmation.

slots.name: quality_concerns
slots.value: Reliability is important, including stable client joining and uninterrupted gameplay; the experience should feel smooth; the system should support troubleshooting and keep networking and standalone modes working as intended.

slots.name: boundary_conditions
slots.value: A player may leave during an active session; the system should handle this gracefully without crashing, but the exact expected behavior is not yet defined.

slots.name: platform_targets
slots.value: The system must support both networked multiplayer play through client applications connected to a game server and standalone play against computer-controlled opponents.

slots.name: network_topology
slots.value: Up to four people can join a shared game through client applications connected to a game server; the system also supports standalone play where a user can play alone with computer opponents.

slots.name: session_flow
slots.value: A session begins with starting a new Mahjong game, players joining until up to four seats are filled, missing seats being filled by computer opponents if needed, play proceeding through managed turns with legal move enforcement and synchronized state, the result being determined and shown at the end, and a new game being able to start afterward.

slots.name: ai_opponent_behavior
slots.value: Computer-controlled opponents must fill unoccupied seats and behave well enough to keep the game playable and allow a valid match to complete.

slots.name: game_rule_variants
slots.value: The baseline Mahjong variant has not yet been decided; the team should choose one standard rule set first, and support for additional regional variants is out of scope for now.

slots.name: mahjong_rule_set
slots.value: The specific Mahjong rule set is undecided and needs verification; one standard baseline variant should be selected before considering others.

slots.name: scoring_and_win_conditions
slots.value: A hand is completed when a player forms a legal winning Mahjong hand under the selected rule set, and the match ends according to that rule set’s scoring and round structure. Exact scoring details are still open pending rule-set selection.

slots.name: rejoin_and_recovery_behavior
slots.value: A disconnected player should have a short reconnection window where their seat is reserved so they can rejoin without disrupting the match; if they do not return in time, the system should replace them with an AI opponent so the game can continue to completion. The match should not end just because of a disconnect unless the remaining state becomes invalid, and brief pausing for reconnect may be allowed.

slots.name: game_state_persistence
slots.value: The system must preserve the full live game state during a disconnect so a returning player can resume exactly where they left off; preserved state includes tile wall or draw state, hands, exposed melds, discard history, turn order, dealer status, and pending action windows.

slots.name: mahjong_rule_set_variant_confirmation
slots.value: The stakeholder has not locked down a specific regional variant and wants the team to choose and confirm one baseline standard before implementation.

slots.name: player_disconnect_policy
slots.value: A player leaving during an active session should be handled as gracefully as possible without crashing; the exact recovery behavior is not yet defined.

slots.name: tile_set_definition
slots.value: The first release should use one standard four-player tile set, but the exact tile composition has not been approved yet and still needs confirmation.

slots.name: scoring_model_details
slots.value: A single scoring model should be defined for the first release, but the exact point values and scoring formula are not yet confirmed.

slots.name: seat_assignment_and_dealer_rules
slots.value: Players should be assigned automatically or allowed to join available seats, and the dealer should be determined at the start and rotated according to the chosen rule set after each hand.

slots.name: game_restart_policy
slots.value: After a match ends, the system should allow a new game to be started.

slots.name: baseline_rule_set_selection_criteria
slots.value: Choose a widely recognized, well-documented standard that is practical to implement, has clear authoritative rules, minimizes ambiguity for the development team, fits the intended audience, and favors delivering a complete reliable product sooner unless the target audience strongly expects a particular regional style.

slots.name: tile_set_composition_confirmation
slots.value: The exact tile set composition is still unconfirmed and must be approved before implementation; the first release is expected to use one standard four-player tile set.

slots.name: scoring_formula_definition
slots.value: The scoring formula is not yet defined; the first release should use a single scoring model, with point values and calculation details to be confirmed later.

slots.name: dealer_rotation_policy
slots.value: Dealer rotation should follow the chosen baseline rule set and be applied after each hand.

slots.name: seat_assignment_policy
slots.value: Seats should be assigned automatically or players should be allowed to join available seats at game start.

slots.name: ai_move_decision_constraints
slots.value: AI-controlled opponents should continue from the preserved game state after takeover and should not alter the underlying hand state; they only change who controls the seat.

slots.name: game_resume_after_disconnect_policy
slots.value: A disconnected player should be given a short reconnection window with their seat reserved; if they do not return in time, the game should continue with an AI replacement, and the match should only end if the remaining state becomes invalid under the chosen rules.

slots.name: reconnection_timeout_duration
slots.value: A short reconnection window is needed, on the order of a couple of minutes, but no fixed timeout has been agreed yet.

slots.name: pause_during_reconnect_policy
slots.value: The match should briefly pause if the disconnected player is the active player, to avoid forcing irreversible actions during the reconnection window.

slots.name: ai_takeover_state_transition_rules
slots.value: If the reconnection timeout expires, the seat should transition from reserved-for-reconnect to AI-controlled, and the game should resume from the current state with no restart.

slots.name: match_validity_after_replacement
slots.value: The match should continue to completion after an AI replacement unless the remaining game state becomes invalid under the chosen rules.

slots.name: turn_pause_state_rules
slots.value: While paused for reconnection, the system should preserve the full live game state and block new turn advancement or irreversible decisions, including current tile wall or draw state, hands, exposed melds, discard history, turn order, dealer status, and pending claim windows.

slots.name: reconnect_pending_action_handling
slots.value: Pending action windows such as claim opportunities must be preserved during a disconnect so the reconnecting player returns to the same decision point; if the timeout expires, the game continues from that preserved state under AI control.

slots.name: ai_takeover_action_authority
slots.value: When AI takes over after timeout, it should control the reserved seat and continue the game from the preserved state without restarting or changing the underlying hand state.
